newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ wool prices fall sharply at Napier.
newsitem.headline: NZ wool prices fall sharply at Napier.

text.p: New Zealand wool prices fell sharply at Thursday's Napier sale, the market indicator falling 20 cents to 415 NZ cents (clean), Wools of New Zealand said.
The strong segment indicator fell 19 cents to 354 cents, and the lamb indicator fell three to 395.
Of the 2,271 clean tonnes on offer, 60 percent was second shear, 13 percent crossbred fleece, 11 percent second shear, bellies and pieces and eight percent lambswool.
The balance was made up of miscellaneous wools. 28 percent of the offer was passed in.
Compared with the last sale at Christchurch on April 3, crossbred fleece, good style and better, fell by up to 2.5 percent, and good to average styles fell by five percent.
Second shear, 37 and 38 micron, fell by up to three percent while 39-40 micron fell by up to five percent.
First lambs wool was on a par to slightly firmer.

Second shear bellies and pieces 35-37 micron, average and average/poor was unchanged. Poor and discoloured fell by 4-5 percent while 39 micron fell by two percent. Interest came from Western Europe, local mills, China, Turkey, India and Australia.
